title: rcb: leakage-aware evaluation of radar cardiorespiratory biometrics
description:
Reference code, feature tables and result files for a re-evaluation of radar cardiorespiratory biometrics on three public datasets (30 dogs, 7.3 GHz ultra-wideband; 110 adults, 60 GHz FMCW; 24 adults, 120 GHz FMCW).

The question is protocol rather than model: how much of a reported cardiorespiratory biometric score survives when window overlap is removed, when the sampling grid is matched, and when a same-species cross-platform control is run alongside the species contrast?

The repository contains the installable rcb package (loaders, filters, 19-D identification and 16-D invariant descriptor sets, multi-bin vital-sign estimator with harmonic notching), the five experiment scripts that generate every table in the manuscript, the figure script, the committed feature tables and result JSONs, 39 unit tests, and a generated number table that maps each quoted value to its result field.

Reported results include: dog heart-rate MAE 7.11 bpm and breathing-rate MAE 1.27 bpm; closed-set identification of 30 dogs at 54.4 % under window-level cross-validation, 46.1 % under a subject-grouped temporal split and 16.3 % at a 25 min horizon; open-set verification at chance (AUROC 0.52-0.59) across 20 random partitions, against 0.949 on one fixed split; dog-vs-human balanced accuracy 86.2 %, smaller than the 93.8 % of a same-species cross-platform control (110 adults at 60 GHz against 24 different adults at 120 GHz).

No raw datasets are redistributed: the three sources are public and cited with DOIs. Feature tables are derived data and are included so the classifiers can be re-run without the raw recordings.
